0.long_answer: Anticonvulsants, also known as antiepileptic drugs or anti-seizure medications, are a diverse group of pharmacological agents used to treat epileptic seizures, including those that occur in individuals with encephalitis. These agents work by suppressing rapid neuronal firing, thereby reducing the abnormal electrical activity that underlies seizures. Their mechanisms often include blocking sodium or calcium channels or enhancing the inhibitory effects of neurotransmitters like GABA, which contributes to stabilizing neuronal membranes and preventing the spread of seizure activity.
